items.title: Eric Alexander interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010
items.q: I found William Paterson — a friend of mine and I found William Paterson college.

ctx.x: You had mentioned yesterday your father listening to you practice, and can’t you play a song all the way through or something. Did you win them over, your parents, with your dedication?

I don’t think my parents really ever knew until later how dedicated I was. Because I think the proof is really in the pudding. And I wasn’t living with them. I was far away from home when this started to happen to me. You know I had periods of time in high school where I would prepare very diligently for a saxophone recital, classical saxophone, I would learn a piece and make big strides and have some effective practice moments. So they knew I was talented. You know all of the teachers would tell them, oh your…
He must have recognized something in you.
